https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/17/leng.text: Menü Kereső A lengyel buszbaleset áldozatai közül hatot sikerült már azonosítani Belföld Nagy Nikoletta Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Hat áldozatot azonosítottak már az M3-ason hajnalban történt lengyel buszbaleset halottjai közül, írja a TVN24 Teresa Kubas-Hulra, a kárpátaljai vajdaság kormányzójára hivatkozva. A hatóságok továbbra is várják a hivatalos megerősítést a további hat áldozattal kapcsolatban. „A konzulátustól, a nagykövetségtől megérkezett az első hat jegyzőkönyv, amelyek megerősítik hat lakosunk halálát” – mondta a kormányzó. Hozzátette, hogy már készítik azokat a csoportokat, amik értesítik majd az áldozatok családtagjait. A hozzátartozók értesítésére létrehozott csoportokban pszichológusok is részt vesznek, hogy támogatást nyújtsanak a családoknak. Közben újabb utasok szólaltak meg a vasárnap hajnali lengyel buszbalesettel kapcsolatban, egyikük azt mondta: az emberek azonnal elkezdtek segíteni egymásnak. Az egyik fiatal zarándok állítólag kitört egy nyílást, amelyen keresztül megkezdhették a sérültek kimentését. A TVN24-nek nyilatkozó túlélő arról beszélt, hogy lábfájdalom miatt a busz padlóján feküdt, és egyszercsak nyugtalanító hangot hallott. „Becsuktam a szemem, és hirtelen furcsa zúgást hallottam” – idézte fel. Néhány pillanattal később már a betört üvegszilánkok és a jármű egyéb darabjai között találta magát. „Valami rám hullott, homok, vagy üveg, valami éles” – mondta. Egy másik túlélő azt mondta, feleségével együtt saját lábán sikerült kijutnia a járműből. „Borzalmas látvány volt. Emberek voltak a busz alatt, kiestek belőle” – mondta a tévének. Már vasárnap is megszólalt a balesetről néhány túlélő , egy borda- és gerincsérülésekkel kórházban fekvő nő kimászott a roncsok alól, majd saját maga húzta ki a húgát a balesetet szenvedett lengyel busz alól, egy férfit is kiszabadított, és összeesett. A nő éppen telefonált, amikor a busz felborult, beütötte a fejét, de nem veszítette el az eszméletét. Látta, ahogy az ülések kiszakadtak a helyükről, az emberek beszorultak a roncsok közé, sikítoztak és segítségért kiabáltak, mondta. Egy zarándoklat résztvevői utaztak hazafelé azon a lengyel turistabuszon, ami egyelőre tisztázatlan okból letért az útról és árokba borult az M3-as autópályán vasárnap éjjel 1 órakor, a rendőrség hivatalos tájékoztatása szerint a balesetben tizenketten meghaltak . A busz utasai lengyel állampolgárok voltak. Maciej Wewiór külügyi szóvivő vasárnap azt mondta, hét sérült állapota nagyon súlyos, további mintegy 40 személy könnyebb sérüléseket szenvedett. A Vajdaságból indult zarándoklat résztvevői hazafelé tartottak Bosznia-Hercegovinából. Marek Konkolewski, a Közúti Közlekedési Főfelügyelőség megbízott helyettes vezetője vasárnap a TVN24-nek azt mondta: ellenőrzést rendelnek el a buszt birtokló cégnél. Azt is mondta, hogy a zarándokok szállítását szervező céget korábban már többször is ellenőrizték, és szabálytalanságokra is fény derült. „Az elmúlt hat évben ennek a cégnek az autóbuszait 11 alkalommal ellenőrizte a Közúti Közlekedési Főfelügyelőség. Kilenc ellenőrzés eredményesen zárult, vagyis az ellenőrök nem találtak hiányosságot vagy szabálytalanságot, két esetben azonban sajnos találtak” – mondta Konkolewski. Az egyik esetben hiányzott a menetíró készülékhez tartozó adatrögzítő lap, a második esetben a munka- és pihenőidőre vonatkozó szabályok betartásában találtak hiányosságokat. A legutóbbi ellenőrzésre 2025. február 25-én került sor. A jasłói Firma Transportowa Michael közlekedési vállalat tulajdonában áll a balesetet szenvedett busz. Korábban Tadeusz Dykasz, a cég tulajdonosa azt mondta , amint értesültek a balesetről, egy pótlóbusszal indultak Magyarországra, hogy a kevésbé súlyosan sérült utasokat Lengyelországba szállítsák. „Mindkét sofőr életben van, egyikük megsérült. Nem tudjuk, mi történt. Nagyon tapasztalt sofőrök, már több éve nálunk dolgoznak. A rendőrség kihallgatja őket” – mondta, hozzátéve, hogy a rendőrségi nyomozás miatt nem férnek hozzá a buszhoz, de együttműködnek a hatóságokkal. Skip next section India's Foreign Ministry slams reports that world leaders fell ill after BRICS summit 09/17/2026 September 17, 2026 India's Foreign Ministry slams reports that world leaders fell ill after BRICS summit India is fending off rumors that multiple world leaders fell ill following the BRICS summit Image: Indian Foreign Ministry/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance India's Ministry of External Affairs has rejected social media claims that several world leaders fell ill after attending the BRICS Summit held in New Delhi on September 12-13, calling the reports "fake" and warning against "malicious" posts. The MEA's fact-checking unit posted on X: "Fake Alert!!! 🚨🚨🚨 We caution against such malicious posts on social media platforms!" This included a social media post by Polymarket, one of the world's largest prediction market platforms. The clarification followed genuine confirmation from South African President Cyril Ramaphosa's office that he had withdrawn from public engagements after returning from the summit, having been advised to rest due to ill health. Separately, unverified posts claimed Chinese President Xi Jinping fainted and left the summit early for medical treatment. The claim originated from Wanjun Xie, chairman of the China Democracy Party, and was not confirmed by Chinese or Indian officials. Beijing has banned the party. Xi is confirmed to have attended the summit and met bilaterally with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. https://p.dw.com/p/5Ml2a Skip next section India vows to protect trade and economic interests amid threat of US's Russia-linked tariffs 09/17/2026 September 17, 2026 India vows to protect trade and economic interests amid threat of US's Russia-linked tariffs Beijing and New Delhi are expected to be the main targets of a new bill on Russian sanctions passed by the US Congress Image: Kevin Lamarque/REUTERS India said Thursday it remains committed to securing energy supplies for its 1.4 billion people and will keep sourcing oil from diverse suppliers, hours after the US House of Representatives passed a bill authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on countries that continue buying Russian oil and gas, including India, along with new sanctions tied to Russia's war in Ukraine. The bill now goes to President Donald Trump for signature. India's Ministry of External Affairs issued a statement responding directly to the legislation: "India remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people. It will continue to do so through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics." The ministry said it had raised the issue with US officials in recent months, adding, "Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side." "The Indian side has also made clear its determination to take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests," the statement added, saying it would work with trade and industry bodies on the legislation's implications. India is the world's third-largest oil importer, and Russia has become one of its largest suppliers as well as a longstanding strategic and military partner. New Delhi has consistently defended the relationship as necessary for its energy needs, resisting outside pressure to scale it back. What do we know about the sanctions? The package targets Russia's energy and defense sectors, President Vladimir Putin and other senior officials. It also targets Moscow's so-called shadow fleet, old tankers it uses to circumvent sanctions. More controversially, the legislation allows Trump to impose secondary sanctions on countries that rely on Russian oil and gas, in the form of tariffs. Beijing and New Delhi are expected to be the main targets of such measures. The bill would also extend sanctions on Iran. Photograph: Win McNamee/Getty Images Donald Trump Analysis Trump beware: US voters are concerned about government corruption Eduardo Porter Alleged self-dealing by the president and his allies doesn’t look so good as corruption emerges as a key issue for midterm voters Government corruption a top issue for US midterm voters, exclusive poll finds Sat 31 Oct 2026 06.00 EDT Last modified on Sat 31 Oct 2026 06.01 EDT Share Voters under 50 probably won’t remember the “ welfare queen ”. But she once embodied Republicans’ claim of the underlying reason for US societal decay: the poor are a bunch of fraudsters. Ronald Reagan introduced Linda Taylor to US voters at a rally during the Republican presidential primary season in 1976. A resident of Chicago’s South Side, Taylor had been arrested for welfare fraud. “She used 80 names, 30 addresses, five phone numbers to collect food stamps, social security, veteran’s benefits for four non-existing deceased veteran husbands,” Reagan said. “Her tax-free cash income alone has been running $150,000 a year.” Taylor may have committed crimes worse than social security fraud. But she wasn’t living on anything near $150,000. Josh Levin, author of The Queen: The Forgotten Life Behind an American Myth, points out that she was only ever charged with stealing $9,000. And yet, Reagan leveraged Taylor’s story to slash spending on welfare, food stamps, Medicaid, public housing and job training. Government corruption a top issue for US midterm voters, exclusive poll finds Read more This woman of color on the bottom rungs of society – born out of a forbidden encounter in the deep south between a white mother and a black father – justified the proposition that to weed out corruption, the first place to look was among the (nonwhite) poor. Half a century on, the Trump administration is dipping into the old imagery to buttress a violent campaign against what’s left of the US’s social safety net, and distract voters from the industrial-scale corruption that is, indeed, sinking America: the self-dealing by the president, his family and his friends. Pages from Reagan’s 1980s playbook are being used to justify initiatives to eviscerate the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (Snap), and government-subsidized health insurance by claiming fraud by less fortunate Americans who, evidently, are learned in the art of grift. The most recent discovery, announced by JD Vance’s anti-fraud taskforce, amounted to $40m defrauded from Snap. “There are people out there who decide to commit fraud against these programs who, quite literally in this case, will steal from the mouths of hungry children in order to enrich themselves,” the vice-president said in Ohio. This came on the heels of Vance’s gleeful announcement that the administration had nixed the health coverage of 760,000 people insured under Obamacare on grounds of fraud. And it meshed nicely with Donald Trump’s offer of a bounty to whoever catches moochers grifting off the government’s dime. “If you turn somebody in, and you, let’s say, report, and you find $1bn, we are giving a commission to that person of 1%,” he said. Trump probably thinks this is smart politics. But Americans are becoming alarmed over the corruption popping up all over the news. An October Harris poll for the Guardian found that government corruption is the second most important issue for voters heading to the polls, second only to the rising cost of living. Eighty-seven percent of respondents to the poll said corruption was a problem, a greater share than those worried about AI or immigration. And yet there’s a hole in the president’s logic. Voters, according to the Harris poll, don’t seem too worried about people getting health insurance on the sly. They are worried about “elected officials putting their own or their donors’ financial interests ahead of the public”. Trump making billions off of crypto would probably fit that concern . Vance has tried to address that complication. He claimed: “I have not seen a single shred of evidence that he participates or sanctions in that corruption.” Vance reminded the electorate that “this guy was a billionaire before he ever got into politics,” which in the vice-president’s mind probably limits Trump’s incentive to stick his hand in the cookie jar. The 65% of voters planning to vote in the midterms who think this corruption is a “major problem”, are unlikely to buy that, though. Last year, the US ranked as the 29th least corrupt nation on the Transparency International Corruption Perceptions Index , a notch below its rank in the last year of the Biden administration and down from 18th in 2016, the year before Trump first came into office. Vance might want to read up on that. Or he might just open his eyes. Trump making $2.2bn in his first year back in office, including $1.4bn from crypto, may not amount to corruption in the narrow sense preferred by his allies on the supreme court, who granted him immunity for any act that might be considered “official”. Trump might not have received direct bribes or agreed to a specific quid pro quo, offering to change policy in exchange for cash. But, just for instance, Trump’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) paused a lawsuit for fraud against a crypto billionaire who had bought $40m worth of $Trump meme coins and invested $75m in another Trump crypto business. Trump nixed the team at the justice department that investigated illegal uses of crypto, and dropped investigations into a variety of crypto companies, including Coinbase, Ripple and Kraken, that contributed to his campaign. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly, for twelve weeks Sign up to How We Win Bernie Sanders, Robert Reich, Stacey Abrams, Mehdi Hasan, Paul Krugman and other bold thinkers on how to defeat Trumpism and build a better future. From our opinion desk. after newsletter promotion The Trump Organization, led by his son Eric, has been cutting deals left and right with regimes that have an indisputable interest in Trump’s foreign policy. A Vladimir Putin-connected oligarch financed a wedding party on a private island for the president’s son, Donald Jr. And Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, is cutting billion-dollar deals with the rulers of countries with which he is conducting diplomacy on behalf of the US. The Democratic congresswoman Rosa DeLauro has compiled a helpful list of the many ways Trump is enriching himself, his family and his allies while in office. It includes: The Qatari government gifted him a luxury jet , potentially violating the emoluments clause of the constitution. The UAE gained access to some tightly guarded, high-end American AI chips soon after an investment firm linked to its ruling family secretly bought a $500m stake in World Liberty Financial, the crypto company funded by the families of Trump and his chum Steve Witkoff. Rich people facing criminal charges have taken to donating to Trump’s political operations and then seeking pardons or clemency. Most recently, Wanda Vázquez Garced , the former governor of Puerto Rico, and the banker who paid her bribes, Julio Herrera Velutini, were pardoned after Velutini’s family gave a $50m deal to Alina Habba, Trump’s former personal lawyer, and donated $3.5m to Trump’s Maga Inc Super Pac. The first family is also making a killing from the government. The Pentagon lent more than $600m to Vulcan Elements, a rare earths startup, just three months after Donald Jr’s venture capital firm 1789 Capital bought a stake in the outfit. Powerus, a drone maker backed by Eric and Donald Jr is selling drone interceptors to Persian Gulf allies of the US that are under attack by Iran, enriching the kids from a misbegotten war launched by the dad without consulting Congress. A British researcher has also built an online tracker documenting hundreds of acts of corruption and abuse of office during Trump’s last 21 months in the White House. The White House denies that the Trump family has ever engaged in any conflicts of interest, and denies granting any pardons or clemency in exchange for political donations. Reagan may have been happy to cut poor Americans adrift. But he wasn’t in it for personal gain. Trump, by contrast, seems to think that going after moochers abusing Snap, offering Maga loyalists a bounty to catch a few, will distract voters from his efforts to leverage his office for cash. Here’s to hoping that US voters – even those inclined to buy into images of undeserving “welfare queens” defrauding government aid programs – can recognize real corruption when they see it.
